A informação foi confirmada pela Direção Nacional de Migrações da Argentina. Em nota, o órgão detalhou que o acesso ocorreu às 22h50 por meio da Ponte Internacional Tancredo Neves, na província de Misiones. Às 23h30, Flávio e família, segundo o governo argentino, embarcaram em um avião privado da companhia Baires Fly e seguiram para Guayaquil, no Equador, conforme informado no plano de voo. Notícias relacionadas: Coordenador de campanha se diz surpreso com fuga de Flávio. “Ato vergonhoso”, diz Lula sobre fuga de Flávio Bolsonaro. Imprensa internacional repercute fuga de Flávio Bolsonaro do Brasil. Ainda de acordo com a Direção Nacional de Migração da Argentina, os quatro apresentaram documentação válida para viagem, sem nenhum impedimento legal para entrar no país. “A travessia foi registrada pela autoridade migratória sem incidentes”, informou o órgão.

news.title: Netanyahu govt has 'attacked' Israeli judicial system, Supreme Court and democratic institutions
news.summary: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Alain Greilsammer, Professor of Political Science at Bar-Ilan University in Tel Aviv. In the wake of the October 7 attacks, regional tensions with Iran, and deepening domestic divisions, Greilsammer argues that the election will be fundamentally shaped by concerns over democratic accountability, judicial independence and the unequal distribution of civic obligations. He warns Netanyahu’s policies risk transforming Israel into “something like an authoritarian or non-democratic state.” He suggests that Israel’s Arab political parties could play a decisive role in determining the election’s outcome.

news.title: Ibrahim Abu Ahmad on Israeli election: 'Crucial for Arab citizens to have ally in Jewish community'
news.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Ibrahim Abu Ahmad, Author, Palestinian Israeli political and peace activist and Head of Social Media for Israel's left-wing Democrats. “Currently, the sentiment in Israel is built around fear and trauma,” explains Ahmad. His most striking observation concerns the apparent contradiction between political leadership and public sentiment: “Many want to see an Arab-Jewish coalition. It's the leadership that is afraid to say it.” Ultimately, he moves beyond conventional electoral calculations to frame Arab-Jewish partnership as a question of democratic survival.
